text: India's Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 replaced the 2016 rules from 1 April 2026 and require four-stream segregation at source: wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste.
source: Lok Sabha statement reported by Deccan Chronicle, 30 Mar 2026

text: According to CPCB data for 2023-24, India generates about 1.85 lakh tonnes of solid waste every day.
source: CPCB 2023-24, as summarised by Vision IAS, 31 Mar 2026

text: Making aluminium from recycled metal needs about 95% less energy than making it from ore.
source: International Aluminium Institute factsheet, 2024 (2019 global data)

text: The 2026 rules rank waste handling as prevention, reduction, reuse, recycling, recovery and disposal, so reuse comes before recycling.
source: Indian Express analysis, summarised by Anantam IAS

text: Special care waste under the 2026 rules includes items like bulbs, batteries and medicines, so they should never go into the wet or dry bin.
source: Drishti IAS summary of the SWM Rules 2026, 29 Jan 2026

text: Bulk waste generators, including large institutions like universities, produce about 30% of India's solid waste and must process wet waste on site or get a responsibility certificate.
source: Drishti IAS summary of the SWM Rules 2026, 29 Jan 2026

text: Sorting waste at the source keeps recyclable material clean, which decides whether it can be recycled later.
source: Indian Express analysis, summarised by Anantam IAS
